Algebra 2 | Quarter 2 | Unit 4: Quadratic Functions

Vertex Form: Peak in Plain Sight

Where and how high does the rider peak?

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 10–11
Topic
Vertex Form
Standards
HSF-IF.C.8a, HSF-BF.B.3, HSA-CED.A.2

Students read the vertex and direction from y = a(x − h)2 + k, write quadratics in vertex form from a vertex and a point, and use vertex form to solve jump problems.

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Read the vertex, axis and direction from vertex form.
  • Describe the transformations a, h and k apply to y = x2.
  • Write a quadratic in vertex form from the vertex and one other point.
  • Solve problems by setting a vertex-form equation equal to a height.

3Essential question

How does vertex form put the most important feature of a jump right in its equation?

5MTB connection

Vertex form is how a jump designer thinks: “I want the rider to peak 2.5 m high, 5 m out.” Those two numbers are h and k, and one more point (the lip) fixes a.

Solving vertex form for a height tells a builder where a rider clears an obstacle, like a 1.6 m tabletop deck.

The mathOn the trail
(h, k)Where and how high the rider peaks
aHow sharply the path curves (speed and gravity)
Solving for a heightWhere the rider clears a feature
Two solutionsRising past it and falling past it
